question: Which food group gives you a double blessing of both plant protein and complex carbohydrates?

options.A: Pure vegetable oils
options.B: Pulses and legumes
options.C: Refined white sugars
options.D: Fresh citrus fruits

explanation: Spot on! Beans, cowpeas, and lentils are fantastic because they give you energy-giving carbs and body-building proteins all in one pot.

question: What is a varicocele, which is a known physical cause of male infertility?

options.A: An infection of the prostate gland
options.B: A blockage of the vas deferens
options.C: Enlarged veins within the scrotum
options.D: The absence of a seminal vesicle

explanation: You got it! Enlarged veins in the scrotum can trap extra heat, which harms healthy sperm production. Easy peasy!

question: What is a fecal impaction?

options.A: A hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum
options.B: An infection of the large intestine lining
options.C: The complete absence of bowel sounds
options.D: A tear in the external anal sphincter

explanation: Fecal impaction happens when dried stool collects and packs tightly in the rectum, blocking normal passage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: What happens to the air left in the lungs after a normal breath (residual volume) as pregnancy advances?

options.A: It fluctuates wildly
options.B: It doubles
options.C: It decreases
options.D: It stays the same

explanation: Because the growing uterus pushes up, there is less room for leftover air trapped in the lungs after breathing out. You are learning fast!

question: Why can waiting for a drop in blood pressure be a sneaky and dangerous way to spot early postpartum bleeding?

options.A: Pregnancy blood volume increases so much that a woman can lose a lot of blood before her BP drops.
options.B: Low blood pressure is completely normal during the first week after birth.
options.C: Postpartum mothers naturally have very high baseline blood pressures.
options.D: Hospital blood pressure machines are almost always inaccurate.

explanation: Because a pregnant woman's body adapts by holding more blood volume, she can lose a dangerous amount before her vital signs suddenly crash. Always watch the bleeding and clinical signs, not just the BP monitor!

question: Which test is primarily used to collect cellular samples for cervical cancer screening?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Pap smear
options.D: Urinalysis strip

explanation: Correct! A Pap smear gently collects cells from the transformation zone to check for any early, unusual changes.

question: What does equity mean in the context of primary health care?

options.A: Only wealthy individuals pay for health services
options.B: Essential health services are accessible to everyone
options.C: Doctors earn the same salary as community health workers
options.D: Every clinic has the exact same amount of money

explanation: Equity ensures fair distribution of health services so that all members of the community can access the care they need, regardless of financial standing. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: A ward manager notices seasonal malaria admissions double every rainy season. What is the best way to use this information?

options.A: Plan ahead to bring in extra temporary staff during rainy months
options.B: Close the ward entirely until the rainy season passes
options.C: Wait until the ward is full and panic
options.D: Reduce nursing shifts to save money for equipment

explanation: Looking at historical trends helps managers forecast busy periods and prepare staff numbers in advance. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which task is typically part of the management role of a PHC nurse manager?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations independently
options.B: Auditing international pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: Overseeing drug inventories and supervising junior health staff
options.D: Writing national health policy legislation

explanation: PHC nurse managers are responsible for supervising staff and managing daily facility logistics like drug stocks. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h7)

question: When would the Ministry of Health use syndromic surveillance?

options.A: When they want to check the exact financial budget of a rural hospital
options.B: When they need the absolute fastest warning about a potential outbreak based on symptoms
options.C: When laboratory tests are cheap and results are ready within minutes
options.D: When they need a complete census of all chronic illnesses

explanation: Syndromic surveillance watches out for symptom groups (like sudden fever and rashes) even before lab results come back, giving us a super-fast early alarm!

question: A local primary school notices many children falling sick due to bushy surroundings and stagnant water. Who is best positioned to mobilize parents to clear the weeds?

options.A: The Parent-Teacher Association
options.B: The school transport drivers
options.C: The national ministry of finance
options.D: The external examination board

explanation: The PTA is the ideal body to mobilize community labor and resources for environmental sanitation tasks around the school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of introducing a new idea for change in healthcare?

options.A: Lowering the salaries of clinical staff
options.B: Increasing the administrative workload of nurses
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital beds
options.D: Improving care delivery and patient outcomes

explanation: We always want our patients to get better! An idea for change is simply a practical way to make nursing care smoother and help patients recover faster.

question: Why does a patient with osteoarthritis usually feel pain in their joint?

options.A: Rapid overproduction of calcium and vitamin D in the blood
options.B: Loss of articular cartilage exposing subchondral bone
options.C: Sudden calcification of the major surrounding ligaments
options.D: Systemic autoimmune attack on the synovial membrane

explanation: When the protective cushion (cartilage) wears away, bone starts rubbing directly against bone. Ouch! That causes the friction and pain.

question: How does good family nutrition directly help a patient managing HIV?

options.A: It cures any underlying opportunistic infections present
options.B: It replaces the need for daily medication intake
options.C: It guarantees an immediate increase in white blood cells
options.D: It strengthens immunity and helps process medications

explanation: Well done! Nutritious meals support overall body strength and help the system tolerate drug regimens successfully.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for improving PTA effectiveness in school health? (Look for the exception)

options.A: Ensuring transparent accounting of all funds raised for projects
options.B: Focusing meetings solely on demanding financial levies without explanations
options.C: Inviting community health nurses to give health talks during meetings
options.D: Partnering with local health centers for regular student screenings

explanation: Focusing only on money without engaging parents in health education or being transparent causes apathy and drives parents away. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why do modern nurse leaders typically combine several management theories instead of using just one?

options.A: All management theories teach the exact same identical concepts
options.B: Hospital accreditation bodies force leaders to memorize all theories
options.C: Healthcare environments are complex and require varied strategies
options.D: It is illegal in most countries to practice only one leadership style

explanation: Because healthcare mixes strict safety rules with human emotions and shifting emergencies, leaders must adapt and mix theories. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h6)

question: How does a negative feedback loop usually react when hormone levels drop too low?

options.A: It signals the endocrine glands to increase hormone production
options.B: It converts stored anabolism into rapid tissue breakdown
options.C: It forces the kidneys to excrete remaining electrolytes
options.D: It shuts down the pituitary gland completely to conserve energy

explanation: Negative feedback works just like an air conditioner thermostat. When levels drop, the body notices and tells the glands to pump out more hormone until balance is restored!

question: What is the difference between anonymity and confidentiality?

options.A: Anonymity means no one can link data to a name; confidentiality keeps known identities secret
options.B: Anonymity is optional in nursing research; confidentiality is strictly mandatory
options.C: Anonymity applies only to secondary data; confidentiality applies to primary data
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical research studies

explanation: Anonymity means nobody (not even the researcher) knows whose data is whose. Confidentiality means you know who they are, but you keep their identity locked away safe.

question: What is the safest tool for a nurse to use when measuring liquid medicine for an infant?

options.A: A regular dining cup
options.B: A standard kitchen teaspoon
options.C: A calibrated oral syringe
options.D: An intravenous syringe

explanation: Household spoons vary wildly in size! A calibrated oral syringe gives us the exact, pinpoint accuracy needed to keep tiny babies safe.

question: What is a major downside of using online questionnaires for hospital patients?

options.A: They prevent researchers from collecting any numerical data
options.B: They force patients to answer every question before submitting
options.C: They always cost significantly more than printed paper surveys
options.D: They may exclude patients who lack internet access or devices

explanation: The digital divide means older or lower-income patients might not have the technology required to complete online forms. Excellent real-world nursing perspective!

question: During which stage of pregnancy do the baby's main organs first form?

options.A: Third trimester
options.B: Right during labor
options.C: First trimester
options.D: Second trimester

explanation: The first trimester is a super busy time when all the major body organs are being built. That's why it's such a delicate period!

question: Why is it so important to use simple, everyday language when teaching mothers at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents mothers from asking questions about immunization schedules
options.B: It ensures clear understanding and correct execution of home care practices
options.C: It saves clinic time so the nurse can finish work much earlier
options.D: It guarantees that mothers will memorize the entire clinic manual

explanation: You nailed it! Clear, jargon-free talk ensures mothers truly understand and can care for their babies safely at home.

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and sudden, rapid dehydration after eating food from a roadside vendor. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Asthma exacerbation
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: You nailed it. Sudden, severe watery diarrhea and rapid dehydration after eating questionable food are classic red flags for cholera. Quick fluid replacement is key here!

question: What does the top number in a blood pressure reading represent?

options.A: Systolic pressure during heart contraction
options.B: Diastolic pressure during heart relaxation
options.C: Mean arterial pressure across the cardiac cycle
options.D: Central venous pressure inside the right atrium

explanation: The systolic (top) number measures the peak pressure in your arteries when the heart pumps. You're mastering the basics! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: A family member is feeding a stroke survivor who can actually hold a spoon with an adaptive grip. What should you do?

options.A: Recommend switching the patient entirely to liquid nutritional supplements
options.B: Praise the family member for providing thorough and efficient care
options.C: Insist that the nurse take over all feeding duties moving forward
options.D: Encourage the patient to use the adaptive spoon independently during meals

explanation: We always want to cheer patients on to do as much as they can for themselves. Independence speeds up recovery!

question: What do we call the thick, yellowish first milk produced right after birth?

options.A: Colostrum
options.B: Lochia
options.C: Surfactant
options.D: Meconium

explanation: Colostrum is like liquid gold for the baby! It's packed with antibodies and nutrients to protect the newborn against early infections.

question: How can community health nurses help lower the number of unsafe abortions?

options.A: By dispelling contraceptive myths and promoting youth-friendly reproductive health services
options.B: By teaching women how to safely use herbal concoctions at home
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal abortions in local villages
options.D: By distributing heavy surgical instruments to traditional birth attendants

explanation: Education and open access to family planning stop unwanted pregnancies before they happen—that is the most powerful prevention!

question: What is the most common primary bone cancer in teens and young adults?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Osteosarcoma
options.C: Chondrosarcoma
options.D: Ewing sarcoma

explanation: Osteosarcoma loves to show up during adolescent growth spurts, usually around the knee area. You've got this!

question: A community nurse visits a home with toddlers and spots an unsafe setup. Which finding needs urgent health teaching?

options.A: Hot cups of tea left sitting right near the edge of the dining table
options.B: A working smoke alarm tested and logged on the kitchen wall
options.C: Chemical cleaners stored high up in a locked utility closet
options.D: Pot handles turned inward toward the back of the stove surface

explanation: Spot on! Hot mugs near table edges are a huge scald trap for toddlers who love to reach up and pull things over.

question: How can a nurse best support self-advocacy in a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: By making all medical and lifestyle decisions on behalf of the patient
options.B: By encouraging the patient to voice their own healthcare choices and rights
options.C: By shielding the patient from interacting with unfamiliar community members
options.D: By filing formal legal complaints without consulting the patient first

explanation: Self-advocacy grows when nurses empower patients to speak up and make their own informed decisions about care and life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h8)

question: What is the main goal of using mobile outreach teams in immunization programs?

options.A: To sell prescription medications directly to rural households
options.B: To reach children living in remote or hard-to-access communities
options.C: To collect taxes from local markets on behalf of the government
options.D: To replace permanent primary health centers in major cities

explanation: You got it! Mobile teams bridge the gap so children in hard-to-reach areas don't miss out on life-saving vaccines.

question: How do the ovaries communicate back to the brain about their hormone levels?

options.A: By altering the physical size of the pituitary gland
options.B: By sending electrical impulses down the spinal cord
options.C: By sending estrogen and progesterone through the blood
options.D: By releasing white blood cells into lymphatic channels

explanation: Ovarian hormones travel through the bloodstream to send feedback signals back to the brain (the hypothalamus and pituitary gland). Simple and amazing how the body works!

question: How does regular physical exercise help lower a person's blood sugar?

options.A: By permanently curing pancreatic beta cell damage
options.B: By destroying excess sugar in the bloodstream
options.C: By increasing insulin sensitivity in muscle cells
options.D: By slowing down overall body metabolism

explanation: Exercise tunes up your muscle cells so they respond better to insulin, helping them pull glucose out of the blood much easier. Keep up the momentum!

question: Why do we treat a blood transfusion with the same high level of caution as an organ transplant?

options.A: It requires permanent immunosuppressive drug therapy
options.B: It can only be performed in major surgical theaters
options.C: It involves the total replacement of the patient's blood
options.D: It involves transferring living tissue that triggers immune responses

question: Which family planning method also protects against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Progestin-only pills
options.B: Subdermal hormone implants
options.C: Copper intrauterine devices
options.D: Barrier methods

explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods are great because they do double duty: they prevent pregnancy and block infections too!

question: What do we call the ongoing health issues that linger for months after recovering from initial COVID-19?

options.A: Post-infectious immunity
options.B: Secondary sepsis
options.C: Acute viral syndrome
options.D: Long COVID

question: Which tool is commonly used to check distant vision during routine school health checks?

options.A: Peak flow meter

question: How do the different types of viral hepatitis mainly differ from one another?

options.A: Only Hepatitis A and B cause physical symptoms, while the rest are completely harmless

options.C: They all share the exact same transmission route through contaminated food and water

question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis?

options.A: To kill all viruses while leaving bacteria alive
options.B: To reduce the total number of common bacteria
options.C: To eliminate every single microorganism and spore
options.D: To remove visible dirt and grease from the skin

question: Why is it so vital for a nurse to keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health assessments?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing barrier methods
options.B: It encourages the patient to share accurate health history and seek care
options.C: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never contract another infection

question: What main factor sets gender-based violence apart from other forms of violence?

options.A: It is directed against someone based on gender roles and inequalities
options.B: It only occurs within marriage and domestic settings
options.C: It is exclusively perpetrated by adult males against adult females
options.D: It involves physical assault without any psychological harm

explanation: You've got this! GBV stems from unequal power balances and societal expectations tied to gender. Recognizing this helps us look beyond just the physical acts.

question: Why do older adults get skin tears and pressure sores so easily?

options.A: Increased sweat gland production softens the skin too much

options.C: High collagen production makes the skin stiff and brittle
options.D: Thinning of the epidermis and loss of subcutaneous fat

question: When body cells are completely cut off from oxygen, what backup energy system do they switch to?

options.A: Oxidative phosphorylation

options.C: Glycolytic synthesis
options.D: Aerobic metabolism

question: Which healthcare professional helps recovering accident victims relearn everyday tasks like dressing, bathing, and eating?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Hospital pharmacist
options.C: Laboratory technician
options.D: Radiology specialist

question: Which of these tiny germs cannot survive on its own and must enter a living host cell to multiply?

options.A: A virus
options.B: A bacterium
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A parasite

explanation: Viruses are tiny! They lack the internal machinery to reproduce by themselves, so they have to hijack a living host cell to make copies. You've got this!

question: How is a 'near miss' different from an adverse event?

options.A: A near miss is caught before reaching the patient, causing no actual harm
options.B: An adverse event never involves medication or treatment mistakes
options.C: An adverse event is only recorded if the patient complains publicly
options.D: A near miss always results in permanent physical disability

explanation: Well done! A near miss is a close call where a mistake almost happened or reached the patient, but was caught in time so nobody got hurt.

question: Which of these is NOT a reliable source for finding new ways to improve care?

options.A: Patient and family feedback
options.B: Scientific evidence

options.D: Direct clinical experience

question: Why does the itching from a scabies infestation usually feel way worse at night?

options.C: Dry night air increases surface skin cracking

question: Why are daily weight checks such an important nursing tool when managing fluid and electrolyte imbalances?

options.A: Body weight dictates the exact dosage of every routine antibiotic

question: What does a low Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) mostly point to during a community screening?

options.A: Normal muscle development
options.B: Risk of acute malnutrition
options.C: Excess visceral fat storage
options.D: Elevated serum cholesterol

question: Which simple tool does a healthcare provider use to actually see a cervical polyp?

options.A: Stethoscope
options.B: Otoscope

options.D: Sphygmomanometer

question: Why must a nurse wash their hands immediately after removing gloves?

options.A: Gloves can have tiny invisible defects and hands can become contaminated during removal
options.B: Soap helps preserve the natural oils in the skin of the hands
options.C: Hospital policy requires handwashing only before putting on gloves
options.D: It removes any lingering powder left inside the glove material

question: What is the main difference between disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization is only used on patient skin, while disinfection is used on metal tools

question: What is the very first thing you do right after pulling the needle out of a patient?

options.A: Activate the needle safety device and drop it into a sharps container
options.B: Recap the needle immediately using both hands for safety
options.C: Massage the injection site vigorously to speed up absorption
options.D: Wipe the skin again with a fresh alcohol swab to clean any blood

explanation: Safety first! Always pop the safety on and drop the used needle straight into the sharps box to protect yourself and others from accidental pricks.

question: A patient receiving regular opioid doses is difficult to wake up and speaks in a sleepy whisper. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Increase the intravenous fluid rate to flush the drug out faster
options.B: Administer a full emergency dose of IV naloxone immediately
options.C: Document that the patient is sleeping peacefully and leave them alone
options.D: Withhold the next scheduled dose and assess breathing depth

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in healthcare?

options.A: To speed up medication administration processes
options.B: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing drugs
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, workers, and communities

explanation: Injection safety is all about making sure no one gets hurt—neither the patient getting the shot, the nurse giving it, nor the wider community! You've got this.

question: Why might a single generic drug molecule have multiple different brand names on the market?

options.A: Generic molecules automatically mutate into different brand substances over time

options.C: Hospitals rename the drugs to avoid confusion with local herbal remedies

question: Where does the front part of the pituitary gland (anterior pituitary) come from during early development?

options.C: An outpouching of the embryonic pharynx called Rathke's pouch
options.D: The mesodermal layer surrounding the developing brain structures

question: How does endocrine hyposecretion usually show up in a patient over time?

options.A: It usually develops slowly over a long period
options.B: It appears suddenly within a few hours
options.C: It fluctuates wildly every single day
options.D: It only occurs after a major surgical operation

explanation: Most of the time, glands get tired or damaged gradually, so symptoms creep up slowly rather than hitting all at once.

question: A nurse sits quietly in the corner of a pediatric playroom to watch children interact without joining in or altering the setting. What kind of observation is this?

options.A: Structured experimental trial
options.B: Non-participant observation
options.C: Unstructured clinical interview

question: Why is it important to investigate the root cause of a workplace accident?

question: What is the main underlying cause of osteoarthritis?

question: What is the best and most direct procedure doctors use to check for a duodenal ulcer?

question: What is the main difference between airborne and droplet transmission?

options.A: Droplet particles can travel for miles across different cities

options.C: Airborne droplet nuclei stay suspended in the air much longer
options.D: Airborne particles only spread through contaminated drinking water

question: Why is the involvement of religious and traditional leaders crucial for eliminating harmful practices?

options.A: They control the primary budgets for hospital construction

options.D: They are legally mandated to act as local health inspectors

question: A patient is prescribed a new transdermal patch for chest pain. What is a crucial step before putting on the fresh patch?

question: A mother on a tight budget needs affordable protein sources for her growing toddlers. Which local foods should the nurse recommend?

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics typically ordered immediately for a patient who has undergone a recent gishiri cut?

question: Why is collaboration with local stakeholders like religious leaders important for nutrition programs?

options.A: They are trusted voices that help mobilize the community

options.C: They manage the international monetary funds for health

explanation: Local leaders command respect and trust, making it much easier to encourage community participation in health initiatives. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h7)

question: What environmental cue tells the pineal gland to slow down melatonin production?

options.B: A drop in body temperature
options.C: Exposure to bright light
options.D: Complete physical exhaustion

question: How should a nurse properly document physical examination findings?

options.B: Let patients write their own clinical findings in the chart
options.C: Record findings objectively using clear measurements and descriptive terms
options.D: Wait until the end of the work week to write all notes at once

question: Why do nurses conduct a community diagnosis before launching a new health program?

options.A: It guarantees that funding from international donors will be approved
options.B: It helps identify the root causes and main health problems of the population
options.C: It allows nurses to avoid interacting directly with community leaders
options.D: It replaces the need for individual patient medical records completely

explanation: You got it! Checking the community first makes sure our interventions actually solve the real problems facing the people there.

question: When is individual dietary counselling most necessary?

options.A: When hospital administrators want to save time on patient education
options.B: When a large community group gathers for a general health seminar
options.C: When teaching basic food hygiene to school children in a classroom
options.D: When a patient has complex medical conditions needing private, tailored care

explanation: Complex conditions like kidney disease require careful, private tailoring of nutrients that group settings cannot provide safely. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h2)

question: You cover an open surgical wound with a sterile dressing. Which part of the infection chain are you primarily blocking?

options.B: Infectious reservoir
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Portal of exit

question: What is the main goal of injection safety protocols in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to patients and protect healthcare workers
options.B: To ensure medications are absorbed faster by the body
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: To speed up medication administration during busy shifts

explanation: Injection safety is all about keeping both sides safe—protecting the patient receiving the injection and keeping you, the nurse, safe from injuries and infections!

question: A nurse is caring for an adult with diabetes who works on a farm. What is the most important health risk to keep an eye on?

options.A: Absence of any need for routine immunization boosters
options.B: Complete resistance to vector-borne diseases
options.C: Increased susceptibility to infections due to chronic illness
options.D: Immediate lifelong immunity acquired from farm work

explanation: Chronic illnesses like diabetes can slow down healing and weaken the immune response, meaning this patient catches infections much more easily.

question: What key tip should you teach a mother giving an oral suspension to her toddler at home?

options.A: Store the open bottle on a sunny kitchen windowsill
options.B: Shake the bottle well immediately before every single dose
options.C: Mix the entire bottle with juice and keep it on the counter
options.D: Stop the medication as soon as the child feels better

explanation: Empowering mothers with good education is key! Reminding them to shake the bottle every time ensures the child gets the exact medicine they need.

question: Why are teenagers so vulnerable to feeling bad about their body image?

options.A: Hormonal imbalances permanently destroy a teenager's self-esteem.
options.B: Rapid physical changes collide with intense social pressure and peer comparison.
options.C: Schools mandate strict physical fitness testing that lowers morale.
options.D: Teenagers naturally lose the ability to regulate their emotional responses.

explanation: True! Puberty brings fast, obvious changes that teens often compare against unrealistic social media standards and their peers.

question: Why would you use an otoscope on a patient complaining of sudden ear pain?

options.A: To inspect the ear canal and eardrum for signs of inflammation or infection
options.B: To test the nerve pathways responsible for hearing sound
options.C: To flush out excess earwax blocking the inner ear
options.D: To measure the exact pressure inside the middle ear cavity

explanation: Ear pain often comes from a little trouble or infection in the canal. Using an otoscope lets you peek right in to see what's going on!

question: What is the best way for a community health nurse to handle local rumors about vaccine safety?

options.A: Engage community leaders in open dialogue and health education
options.B: Ignore the community complaints and focus only on paperwork
options.C: Scold parents who ask questions about vaccine ingredients
options.D: Close down the immunization clinic until rumors stop spreading

explanation: Teaming up with trusted community leaders and providing respectful, clear health talks is the best way to clear up fears and build trust.

question: What is the standard metric unit for measuring liquid volume in the ward?

options.A: Drop
options.B: Grain
options.C: Pound
options.D: Milliliter

explanation: Liters and milliliters (mL) are our go-to units for measuring liquid medications and IV fluids every day.

question: Which government tier is primarily responsible for managing Primary Health Care centers?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Private pharmaceutical boards
options.C: International donor agencies

explanation: Primary health care services in Nigeria are closest to the grassroots and are managed by the local government authorities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which Nigerian legislation sets the legal age of marriage at eighteen years?

options.A: The National Health Act

question: In cervical cell changes, what makes CIN 3 more serious than the earlier stages?

options.C: Invasion through the basement membrane has already occurred

question: What does asking a patient to smile and puff out their cheeks help evaluate?

options.A: Cranial nerve I
options.B: Cranial nerve II
options.C: Cranial nerve VII
options.D: Cranial nerve VIII

question: What is the maximum score for the verbal (talking) category in a fully alert adult?
explanation: The verbal score ranges from 1 to 5. Scoring a 5 means your patient is fully alert and oriented to time, place, and person.

question: A nurse is preparing to give a 10:00 AM medication dose using the unit dispensing cart. When is the best time to document that the drug was given?

options.A: Whenever the nurse remembers during the afternoon visiting hours
options.B: Before leaving the central pharmacy room with the mobile drug cart
options.C: Immediately after the patient swallows the medication at the bedside
options.D: At the end of the shift when all patient charts are gathered together

explanation: Documentation must happen right after administration to prevent accidental double-dosing or missed records. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main role of a nurse when it comes to ward medical supplies?

options.A: Setting the market prices for incoming hospital drugs
options.B: Manufacturing basic pharmaceuticals for emergency use
options.C: Auditing the financial statements of the hospital board
options.D: Acting as a primary gatekeeper and user of resources

explanation: You handle drugs and supplies right at the bedside every day, which means you play a huge part in monitoring and using them wisely. Great job keeping track of how resources are managed!

question: What is the safest nursing action right before giving a calculated dose of liquid medicine to a child?

options.A: Administer the drug immediately without checking the patient ID band
options.B: Triple the dose to ensure the infection clears faster
options.C: Ask the child's older sibling if the amount looks correct
options.D: Have another nurse independently verify the weight-based calculation and dose

explanation: Four eyes are better than two! Having a colleague double-check weight-based math prevents medication errors and keeps pediatric patients safe.

question: How do scientists use bacteria like E. coli in modern recombinant DNA technology?

options.A: To destroy unwanted chemical impurities inside synthetic drug vials
options.B: To serve as natural painkillers harvested during fermentation
options.C: To extract raw mineral salts directly from underground rock beds
options.D: To act as biological factories that produce human proteins like insulin

explanation: By putting human genes into bacteria, scientists turn them into tiny biological factories that safely pump out human proteins like insulin.

question: As a nurse, what is the quickest way to help a patient who is suddenly struggling to catch their breath due to lung cancer?

options.A: Laying the patient flat on their back in bed
options.B: Placing the patient in a high-Fowler's position
options.C: Encouraging rapid, shallow mouth breathing
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake for twelve hours

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Sitting the patient upright in a high-Fowler's position lets their chest expand fully, making it much easier to draw breath.

question: Which nursing action compromises the accuracy of a fluid balance chart?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to guess and write down intake amounts
options.B: Involving the patient and family in reporting oral drinks
options.C: Converting all cup and bowl volumes into milliliters promptly
options.D: Notifying the doctor immediately about a sudden drop in urine output

explanation: Relying on memory causes missed entries and incorrect data that jeopardize patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h8)

question: Which two hormones easily cross into the brain to cause changes during pregnancy?

options.A: Cortisol and adrenaline
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

question: Why do nurses use transmission-based precautions?

options.A: To stop the spread of specific targeted pathogens
options.B: To replace standard handwashing routines entirely
options.C: To isolate healthy staff members from routine work
options.D: To reduce hospital utility and cleaning costs

explanation: You've got this! These extra precautions are added on top of standard care whenever we are dealing with known or suspected germs that need special containment. Great job!

question: How does early palliative care help a patient going through tough cancer treatments?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any surgical operations
options.B: It lowers hospital bills by shortening surgical procedures
options.C: It focuses on relieving symptoms, pain, and emotional distress
options.D: It guarantees that the cancer will completely disappear

explanation: Palliative care is all about comfort, helping patients manage tough physical and emotional symptoms every step of the way. You are doing wonderful work today!

question: What is the most sensitive daily indicator of fluid balance in a patient with acute renal failure?

options.A: Total daily fluid intake calculations
options.B: Skin turgor and mucous membrane check
options.C: Daily body weight measurement
options.D: Blood pressure readings every four hours

explanation: Weighing the patient daily is the most accurate way to detect rapid fluid gains or losses, where one kilogram equals one liter of fluid. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which condition is a major newborn risk specifically prevented by strict cord hygiene and clean cutting tools?

options.A: Respiratory distress syndrome
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Neonatal tetanus
options.D: Congenital heart defects

explanation: Clostridium tetani spores enter through unhygienic umbilical cord stumps, making clean tools and ties crucial for prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h5)

question: A 14-year-old patient starts dressing and speaking just like a new group of friends. How should you as a nurse view this?

options.A: An indication of developmental delay in cognitive reasoning
options.B: Evidence of negative peer pressure that requires institutionalization
options.C: A sign of severe psychological personality splitting
options.D: A normal part of peer bonding and identity exploration

explanation: Fitting in with friends is a healthy part of growing up. They are just trying out different styles to see what feels right!

question: What does 'loss to follow-up' mean in the context of a longitudinal prospective study?

options.A: Nurses forget to check the patient's vital signs during a routine shift

options.C: Researchers accidentally delete all computer files from the first day of the study
options.D: The hospital misplaces the budget allocated for patient transportation

explanation: Attrition threatens study validity when participants who leave differ systematically from those who stay until the final evaluation. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why does parental apathy pose a serious problem for the PTA?

options.A: It forces the government to close down all private hospitals
options.B: It automatically increases the academic salaries of teachers
options.C: It leads to poor attendance and lack of support for school programs
options.D: It stops students from participating in sports competitions

explanation: When parents show little interest in meetings, collective decision-making and community-driven projects fail to take off. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h6)

question: What does 'self-financing' mean for a DRF scheme?

options.A: It generates enough revenue from sales to buy replacement stock
options.B: It borrows money from private banks whenever stocks get low
options.C: It relies entirely on yearly donations from foreign countries
options.D: It receives unlimited free drugs from the central ministry

explanation: Great job! Self-financing just means the fund keeps itself alive through patient payments instead of waiting for outside help.

question: Which measure is most effective for controlling infectious diseases in a school setting?

options.A: Removing all washing facilities from school grounds
options.B: Banning all outdoor sports activities permanently
options.C: Isolating children in windowless rooms all day
options.D: Promoting proper hand hygiene and immunization checks

explanation: Handwashing and verifying immunization records are proven, frontline defenses against the spread of infections among children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which symptom during the final months of pregnancy strongly points to placenta previa?

question: How do community nurses best advocate for marginalized or vulnerable populations?

options.A: By reporting undocumented migrants to law enforcement agencies
options.B: By advising them to relocate to wealthier neighborhoods
options.C: By setting up mobile clinics and offering free health screenings
options.D: By closing down rural health posts to save money

question: Why is asking about family bleeding history so important before a circumcision?

options.A: To check if the patient is allergic to local numbing medications

options.C: To predict how fast the surgical wound will grow new skin cells
options.D: To screen for clotting disorders like hemophilia that could cause excessive bleeding

explanation: Safety first! Screening for bleeding disorders helps catch conditions like hemophilia early, preventing dangerous and uncontrolled bleeding after the cut is made.

question: Why must a nurse never turn their back on an open sterile field?

options.A: The sterile items will immediately slide off the tray
options.B: It looks unprofessional to the patient
options.C: You cannot see if something unsterile contaminates it
options.D: Air currents will blow the sterile drape away

question: How far do infectious respiratory droplets typically travel through the air?

options.A: Throughout the ventilation system
options.B: Up to ten meters
options.C: Across an entire building
options.D: Less than one meter

question: Why do doctors test breast cancer tissue for HER2 receptors?

question: What is a major characteristic of passive immunity?

options.A: It stimulates the bone marrow to produce permanent memory cells.

options.C: It provides immediate protection that fades relatively quickly.

question: Which physical sign is most commonly associated with iron deficiency anemia?

options.D: Pale conjunctiva inside the lower eyelids

question: A patient taking an estrogen antagonist for breast cancer complains of hot flashes. What is the best nursing response?

question: What is usually the main symptom of a small, uninfected vulval cyst?

question: What is the primary purpose of a general physical examination?

options.A: To diagnose complex psychiatric disorders independently
options.B: To replace the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.C: To prescribe appropriate pharmacological interventions
options.D: To gather baseline data about a patient's health status

question: Which item is a major source of hidden sodium in many Nigerian home-cooked meals?

question: Why is keeping track of a home care patient's weight so important over time?

question: What essential check must a nurse perform immediately after removing an IV catheter?

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is common in advanced bone tumors due to rapid bone breakdown?

question: What was the main discovery of the Hawthorne Studies regarding workers?

question: Why are non-pain symptoms considered just as important to manage as pain in palliative patients?

question: What happens to the body during the stage of exhaustion under long-term, chronic stress?

question: Why are narrow-spectrum antibiotics preferred when you know the exact germ causing the trouble?

options.A: They work much faster than broad-spectrum drugs
options.B: They never cause allergic reactions in patients
options.C: They can be taken without water
options.D: They cause less harm to normal body flora

question: What famous milestone did James Lind achieve when he tested citrus fruits on sailors?

options.A: The chemical isolation of pure vitamin C in a laboratory

question: Which of these is a classic example of a microvascular (small blood vessel) complication of diabetes?

question: What is a vulval cyst?

question: Where should you look in a published study to find the actual numbers and statistical findings?

question: Why is the nurse often called the 'final safeguard' in medication administration?

question: Which specific antidote is given to protect the liver during a dangerous paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

question: Which eye condition means a patient should NEVER take anticholinergic drugs?

question: Why do nurses ask patients about how many pads or tampons they use when assessing heavy periods?

question: A patient who tested positive for a late-onset degenerative disorder expresses severe anxiety about the future and refuses to talk to family. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

question: You just gave an injection on a busy ward. What is your very next step with that used needle?

question: What happens during the acrosome reaction?

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care (ANC) services for a pregnant mother?

question: How does active listening help prevent sexual difficulties in a relationship?

question: Why does the amygdala let you react to danger before you even have time to think?

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four central concepts in the nursing metaparadigm?

question: Which physical sign is commonly seen during the active dying phase?

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention?

options.D: When a mild headache needs to be relieved over an eight-hour period.

question: Which of the following practices regarding alcohol is safest for a nursing mother?

options.A: Consuming alcohol immediately before every single nursing session to relax the baby
options.B: Mixing alcohol directly into infant formula to help the baby sleep through the night
options.C: Drinking large amounts of beer daily because it is traditionally believed to boost milk supply
options.D: Avoiding heavy or frequent drinking and waiting several hours after a drink before nursing

explanation: Alcohol enters breast milk quickly, so minimizing intake and allowing time for the body to clear it protects the infant. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h7)

question: What do we call patches of diseased bowel separated by areas of normal, healthy tissue in Crohn's disease?

options.A: Crypt abscesses
options.B: Skip lesions
options.C: Fistula tracts
options.D: Brush borders

explanation: Think of them as 'skipping' spots! Crohn's is famous for patchy patterns where diseased areas sit right next to healthy tissue.

question: Which medication do doctors commonly start early in pregnancy to help prevent pre-eclampsia in women with sickle cell disease?

options.A: High-dose hydroxyurea
options.B: Low-dose aspirin
options.C: Therapeutic penicillin
options.D: Intravenous iron sucrose

explanation: Brilliant! Low-dose aspirin is a helpful tool started early on to protect the placenta and lower the risk of pre-eclampsia.

question: Which of these is an environmental risk factor for adolescent injury?

options.A: Late developmental puberty
options.B: A family history of hypertension
options.C: A quiet and supportive home
options.D: Lack of safe recreational spaces

explanation: Spot on! Environmental risk factors involve the physical surroundings and community spaces—like unsafe streets or no play areas—that increase danger.

question: An elderly patient with less muscle and more body fat takes a water-soluble drug. What is the likely result?

options.A: The drug spreads out forever and disappears
options.B: The drug instantly turns into a fat-soluble chemical
options.C: The drug fails to enter the bloodstream at all
options.D: The drug concentrates in a smaller fluid volume, leading to higher blood levels

explanation: Water-soluble drugs dissolve in body water. Since older adults usually have less total body water, a standard dose will be much more concentrated!

question: How is a middle-range theory different from a grand nursing theory?

options.A: It is completely unproven and used only by student researchers
options.B: It applies strictly to hospital administration rather than patient care
options.C: It avoids using any concepts related to human behavior
options.D: It focuses on specific, manageable clinical situations rather than broad, universal ideas

explanation: Exactly. While grand theories try to explain all of nursing, middle-range theories zoom in on specific, everyday clinical situations that are easier to study.

question: How does a typical resting tremor look in a patient with early Parkinson's disease?

options.A: As rhythmic head nodding that worsens only during high-stress situations
options.B: As violent shaking of both arms when reaching out to grab an object
options.C: As a pill-rolling movement of the thumb and forefinger when the hand is relaxed
options.D: As sudden muscle jerks throughout the entire body during deep sleep

explanation: Picture someone gently rolling a tiny pill back and forth between their thumb and index finger while resting—that's the classic Parkinson's resting tremor!

question: Which clinical sign suggests that a newborn with a skull injury may have underlying intracranial pressure?

options.A: A strong grip reflex in both hands
options.B: Rapid passage of meconium stool
options.C: A high-pitched cry and lethargy
options.D: An intense craving for frequent feeds

explanation: Neurological irritability, altered levels of consciousness like lethargy, and a high-pitched cry are classic indicators of increased pressure inside the cranium. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h4)

question: Through which structure must a flatus tube pass to enter the rectum?

options.A: The anal sphincters
options.B: The pyloric sphincter
options.C: The duodenal ampulla
options.D: The ileocecal valve

explanation: To enter the rectum safely, the tube needs to pass through the internal and external anal sphincters. You've got this!

question: Why is community outreach by nurses and midwives so vital for family planning programs?

options.A: It helps engage local leaders and dismantle cultural stigma against modern methods.
options.B: It allows health workers to bypass government health policies entirely.
options.C: It ensures that nurses can collect financial levies from local households.
options.D: It replaces the need for clinical examinations inside health facilities.

explanation: Spot on! Going out into the community builds trust, involves local leaders, and helps clear up cultural or religious worries right at the grassroots level.

question: What do we call a strange, unexpected drug reaction that happens because of a patient's unique genetics?

options.A: Therapeutic side effect
options.B: Anaphylactic shock
options.C: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.D: Cumulative toxicity

explanation: Idiosyncratic means it's a rare, one-of-a-kind reaction that catches everyone by surprise based on body chemistry.

question: Why is the waiting time before checking for infertility shortened to just 6 months for women aged 35 and older?

options.A: The uterus shrinks and cannot hold a pregnancy safely
options.B: Older women have more chronic infections in the pelvis
options.C: Hormone levels drop to zero immediately after thirty-five
options.D: Ovarian reserve and egg quality decline rapidly after this age

explanation: Spot on! A woman's biological clock ticks a bit faster in her mid-thirties, so catching any issues early helps make treatments much more successful. You're learning fast!

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do with a mechanical weighing scale before a patient steps on it?

options.A: Wipe the platform with hot cooking oil
options.B: Place a thick mat underneath it
options.C: Lock the height rod permanently
options.D: Calibrate and balance it to zero

explanation: Always check that the scale starts right at zero! This ensures your weight reading is accurate and not thrown off by a previous reading.

question: Which category of workplace hazard includes exposure to loud machinery noise and extreme heat?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Chemical hazards
options.C: Psychosocial hazards
options.D: Biological hazards

explanation: Noise, vibration, radiation, and extreme temperatures are classified as physical workplace hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of 'sensate focus' exercises in sex therapy?

options.A: To replace all forms of verbal communication between partners
options.B: To test the physical endurance of the cardiovascular system
options.C: To eliminate performance anxiety by removing the pressure of intercourse
options.D: To increase muscular strength in the lower pelvic floor

explanation: Sensate focus helps couples slow down and reconnect through gentle touch, taking away the stressful expectation of sexual performance.

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: Providing financial aid to grieving families
options.B: Curing the underlying terminal disease completely
options.C: Speeding up the natural dying process safely
options.D: Improving the quality of life for patients and families

explanation: Think of palliative care as a comforting blanket. Its main goal is to bring peace, ease pain, and support both the patient and their loved ones through a tough time.

question: Why should you give extra time when doing a mental assessment on an older adult?

options.A: Rushing can cause anxiety and lead to inaccurate assessment results
options.B: Older adults legally require thirty minutes per interview question
options.C: It gives the nurse time to complete paperwork during the session
options.D: Slowing down prevents the patient from hearing the questions

explanation: Thinking takes a little longer with age, so patience helps you get accurate answers and keeps the patient calm.

question: Why is active severe diarrhea a major drawback for using rectal suppositories?

options.A: It causes the suppository to dissolve instantly into gas
options.B: The body will expel the medication before it has time to absorb
options.C: It forces the drug to bypass the liver too quickly
options.D: The medication will turn the stool a bright toxic color

explanation: Frequent bowel movements push the medication right back out before the mucous membrane can absorb the drug. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h6)

question: A patient has extremely dry, thick skin on their heels and soft, hydrated skin on their inner arm. Where will a topical cream absorb the fastest?

options.A: On the heel because it has more subcutaneous fat
options.B: On the inner arm because the skin is soft and hydrated
options.C: Absorption rate will be identical in both locations
options.D: On the heel because thick skin holds more medication

explanation: Hydrated skin and thinner skin barriers allow topical agents to penetrate much faster than dry, thick areas like the heels. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h2)

question: How should you respond if a newly diagnosed visually impaired patient feels angry, sad, or hopeless?

options.A: Inform them that crying will only make their eye pressure worse
options.B: Tell them to stop worrying because things could be much worse
options.C: Acknowledge and validate their feelings as a normal part of grieving
options.D: Change the subject immediately to avoid upsetting them further

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Losing vision is a huge life change, and validating their emotions helps them process the grief and move toward healing.

question: A patient has an injury damaging the nerve fibers in their ventral root. What would you expect to see?

options.A: Inability to move the target muscle effector
options.B: Inability of receptors to detect hot temperatures
options.C: Loss of sensation to pinprick in the skin
options.D: Total loss of conscious thought and memory

explanation: Since the ventral root carries the outgoing 'action' command to muscles, damaging it blocks that final signal, leading to weakness or trouble moving.

question: What is the main job of anabolism in the body?

options.A: Breaking down large food particles into waste
options.B: Destroying damaged cells through natural pathways
options.C: Building complex molecules from simpler ones
options.D: Releasing stored heat directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Think of anabolism as the builder! It takes small building blocks and puts them together to form larger, complex molecules, just like building a house with bricks.

question: Why do we apply a tourniquet to a patient's arm before trying to insert an IV cannula?

options.A: To sterilize the outer skin surface before cleaning
options.B: To completely stop arterial blood flow to the limb
options.C: To numb the local skin area and reduce sharp pain
options.D: To trap venous blood and make the veins swell up

explanation: Exactly! The tourniquet pauses blood from returning to the heart, causing the veins underneath to plump up so they are much easier to see and feel.

question: A lecturer leaves an anatomical chart displayed on the board long after the topic has changed to nursing ethics. What mistake has the lecturer made?

options.A: Poor timing and management of visual distraction
options.B: Failing to check the cost of the material
options.C: Using an inaccurate scientific model
options.D: Selecting a non-projected visual aid

explanation: Leaving media displayed after the discussion has moved on distracts learners and dilutes the focus of the current lesson. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h5)

question: Why should you check if a patient has recently passed stool before giving a suppository?

options.A: Stool presence guarantees that the drug will be absorbed twice as fast
options.B: A full rectum can block the medication from contacting the mucosal wall
options.C: Bowel movements prevent the nurse from wearing disposable gloves
options.D: Empty bowels mean the patient is allergic to the prescribed drug

explanation: If the rectum is full of stool, the suppository won't touch the lining properly, reducing drug absorption.

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement (QI) in nursing?

options.A: Cutting down nursing staff to reduce hospital costs
options.B: Punishing staff who make medication mistakes
options.C: Filing incident reports after safety errors happen
options.D: Proactively redesigning care to give patients better outcomes

explanation: Great job thinking ahead! Quality improvement is all about fixing systems before errors happen, rather than just reacting after things go wrong. You've got this!

question: A male patient with a pelvic fracture has blood at the tip of his penis and cannot urinate. What is the safest nursing action?

options.A: Hold off on placing a standard urinary catheter and report the finding immediately.
options.B: Massage the lower abdomen firmly to force the patient to void naturally.
options.C: Insert a rigid plastic catheter gently until resistance disappears.
options.D: Force a standard Foley catheter past the blockage to relieve the bladder pressure.

explanation: Never force a catheter if you suspect a torn urethra—it can make the injury much worse! Always pause, leave it alone, and inform the doctor right away.

question: What is the number one thing that encourages young people to open up and share sensitive health info with a nurse?

options.A: Free mobile phones
options.B: Presence of tribal leaders
options.C: Free meals at the clinic
options.D: Guaranteed confidentiality

explanation: Trust is everything! Teens need to know their secrets are safe with you before they'll feel comfortable talking about their health.

question: Why is the initial binding between sperm and egg membrane proteins so important?

options.A: It immediately triggers the shedding of all female chromosomes
options.B: It stops the sperm from releasing any digestive enzymes
options.C: It ensures species-specific recognition before the cell membranes can fuse
options.D: It permanently seals the uterus against outside infections

explanation: The proteins act like a security check, making sure human sperm matches with a human egg before letting cell fusion happen.

question: Who is typically a member of a Health Facility Development Committee?

options.A: Health workers and community representatives
options.B: International pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.C: Federal ministers of finance and education
options.D: State governors and local government chairmen

explanation: The HFDC brings together the people working inside the clinic and the community members using the services to ensure smooth daily operations. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why might a woman with Type III FGM need a procedure called defibulation during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent severe postpartum hemorrhage from the uterus
options.B: To allow the baby to pass through the narrowed vaginal opening
options.C: To correct an underlying urinary tract infection
options.D: To speed up the delivery of the placenta

explanation: Spot on! The scar tissue seal blocks the birth canal, so healthcare providers must surgically open the area during labor to keep mother and baby safe.

question: What is the main goal of Family Life Education in the community?

options.A: Promoting overall well-being and disease prevention
options.B: Treating acute medical and surgical emergencies
options.C: Managing chronic hospital admissions
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders in infants

explanation: Family Life Education is all about helping people stay healthy and preventing problems before they start, rather than treating emergencies.

question: Which diagnostic test is primarily used to confirm the location of a suspected ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Abdominal X-ray scan
options.C: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: A transvaginal ultrasound allows the healthcare provider to look directly inside the uterus and fallopian tubes to see where the pregnancy has implanted. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h5)

question: What is the main job of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine when given during shock?

options.A: Dissolving blood clots inside blocked arteries
options.B: Dilating peripheral airways to ease breathing
options.C: Lowering heart rate to reduce cardiac workload
options.D: Constricting blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors squeeze ('press') the blood vessels, tightening up the pipes to raise the blood pressure and keep vital organs perfused when the patient's own pressure is tanking.

question: Which of these is a major barrier to healthcare access in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Severe shortage of health facilities and poor road networks
options.B: Instant availability of advanced surgical equipment
options.C: Too many well-trained medical doctors per capita
options.D: Excessive number of specialized tertiary hospitals

explanation: Correct! Bad roads and faraway clinics make getting to a hospital a massive challenge for rural villagers.

question: Even after physical withdrawal fades, why is quitting smoking still so tough?

options.A: Commercial cigarettes contain permanent cellular dyes
options.B: Social laws make it illegal to stop smoking abruptly
options.C: The body continues producing natural nicotine forever
options.D: Psychological habits and environmental triggers remain deeply ingrained

explanation: The mental habit and social triggers stick around long after the physical chemicals leave the body. Don't worry if this takes time to master!

question: What is the classic ECG sign that a heart muscle is currently injured (like in a heart attack)?

options.A: Prolonged QT interval
options.B: Flattened P waves
options.C: Shortened PR interval
options.D: ST segment elevation

explanation: When that ST segment lifts up off the line, it's a major red flag telling us the heart muscle is stressed and lacking oxygen.

question: Which patient position is standard and most appropriate for rectal medication administration?

options.A: Prone face-down position
options.B: High Fowler's position
options.C: Sims' position
options.D: Supine flat position

explanation: Sims' position (left lateral with the top leg flexed) naturally exposes the anus and follows the anatomical curve of the lower intestine. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the big advantage of giving tumor chemotherapy through an artery instead of a vein?

options.A: It completely eliminates all side effects throughout the entire body
options.B: It delivers a higher concentration of the drug directly to the tumor site
options.C: It prevents the drug from ever entering the systemic circulation
options.D: It allows the patient to take the chemotherapy medication at home

explanation: Think of it like dropping the medicine right on the doorstep of the problem! It gives the tumor a concentrated dose before the blood carries it away.

question: What is key to getting staff members to gladly accept a newly introduced management decision?

options.A: Immediate disciplinary action for anyone who asks questions
options.B: Clear communication of the reasons behind the change
options.C: Changing the shift roster every single day without notice
options.D: Keeping all details of the new policy hidden from view

explanation: When nurses understand the 'why' behind a new policy, they are far more likely to support it and work together.

question: Which set of vital signs shows that a patient's circulation is collapsing from an allergy?

options.A: Low heart rate and low blood pressure
options.B: High heart rate and low blood pressure
options.C: Low heart rate and high blood pressure
options.D: High heart rate and high blood pressure

explanation: As blood pressure drops, the heart beats much faster to try and make up for it and keep blood flowing.
